title: Analysis-Japan’s $15 billion Rapidus chip bet hinges on winning customers
key_facts: Rapidus has $15B in state backing and plans 2nm production in the second half of next fiscal year.
It said Monday it will partner with 17 companies including Synopsys and Infosys to help customers design chips.
Analyst Nori Chiou: the biggest question is who will fill the fab; Monday's announcement is not evidence of commercial traction.
Only TSMC, Samsung and Intel make 2nm chips now.
Rapidus works with IBM and has started pilot operations.
Rapidus targets an IPO around the year ending March 2032.
Japan's share of global chip market fell from about 50% in the 1980s to under 10%.
quote_evidence: The biggest question for Rapidus is still who will actually fill the fab.
Running a chip fab around the clock, maintaining stable, consistent yields and continuing production in a way that makes the business viable is extremely difficult.
Preparations for mass production were progressing on schedule.
why_it_matters_hint: Rapidus must prove it can win customers and make advanced chips.
